predecessors.name: Zirid dynasty
predecessors.text: Tripolitania: 'After 1001, Tripolitania broke away from Zirid control under the leadership of Fulful ibn Sa'id ibn Khazrun'

successors.name: Kingdom of Africa
successors.text: Tripoli, which Roger II 'finally' captured 'in 1146 or 1147' after the inhabitants expelled the Banu Khazrun

ledger.x: c. 1075: al-Muntasir takes Hammadid lands. 'Sometime around 1075, al-Muntasir led the Banu Adi' against the Hammadid kingdom and took 'Ashir, al-Masila, the M'zab and Righ regions, and a base at Waghlana near Biskra'.

wars.name: Khazrunid war against the Zirids
wars.outcome: 'Between 1038 and 1049, he waged a long war against the Zirids'; Khalifa launched attacks 'in the regions around Gabès and Tripoli' (no year); 'During the invasions of the Banu Hilal in 1051-1052, he accepted the authority of al-Mu'izz ibn Badis'.

wars.name: Al-Muntasir's raid on the Hammadids
wars.outcome: Around 1075 al-Muntasir led the Banu Adi against the Hammadid kingdom and took Ashir, al-Masila, the M'zab and Righ regions and a base at Waghlana near Biskra; the Hammadid governor of Biskra later had him killed.

wars.name: Roger II's attempts on Tripoli
wars.outcome: Roger II 'initiated an expedition in 1143 with the objective of capturing Tripoli', which 'was unsuccessful because the neighboring Banu Khazrun tribes staunchly defended the city' (infobox: Khazrunid victory, commander Muhammad ibn Khazrun); a famine drove…

certainty.note: The page names Tripoli, Tripolitania and a few Hammadid towns, with no frontier; the 120 km circle and the Hammadid provinces are the researcher's.
